meta.name: Tartine Lemon Cream Tart
meta.yields: 12 tartlets (10cm / 4in) — dough batch makes all 12, bake as many as needed and freeze remaining discs
meta.description: Tartine's signature lemon tart: buttery pate sucree shell filled with Pierre Herme-style lemon cream (butter mounted into curd for a softer, more unctuous texture than standard curd), topped with whipped cream. Dough recipe from Boulangerie Artisanale des Maures in southern France.

change_log.summary: Granular curd steps: strain juice, water bath, combine, cook, strain curd, cool, mount butter. Press-in tartlet option. Immersion blender only.
Adapted for 10cm tartlets: per-stage mise en place, 12x88g dough portions, tartlet bake times
Initial recipe from Tartine Bakery cookbook (sweet tart dough + lemon cream + assembly)

vessels.name: Stainless-Steel Bowl
vessels.reuse: Double boiler curd -> mount butter -> pour into shell

states.title: Cream Butter, Sugar & Salt
states.direction: Using stand mixer fitted with paddle attachment, combine 255g room-temperature butter, 200g sugar, and 1.5g salt. Mix on medium speed until smooth.
states.exit_condition: Mixture is smooth and uniformly combined, no visible butter chunks

notes.text: Butter must be truly room temp — soft enough to indent easily with a finger but not greasy or melting.

states.title: Add Eggs
states.direction: Mix in 1 egg on medium speed. Add remaining egg and mix until smooth. Stop mixer and scrape down sides of bowl with rubber spatula.
states.exit_condition: Eggs fully incorporated, mixture smooth, bowl sides scraped clean

notes.text: Eggs can be brought to room temp quickly by submerging in lukewarm water for 5 minutes.

states.title: Add Flour
states.direction: Add 500g flour all at once. Mix on low speed just until incorporated.
states.exit_condition: Flour just incorporated — no dry patches, no overmixing. Dough cohesive but not elastic.

notes.text: Do not overmix — stop the moment flour disappears. Overmixing develops gluten and makes the dough tough rather than tender.

states.title: Divide & Shape Discs
states.direction: On a lightly floured surface, divide dough into 12 equal portions (~88g each). Shape each into a ball, then flatten into a disc 12mm thick. Wrap each disc individually in plastic wrap.
states.exit_condition: 12 evenly sized discs (~88g each), each 12mm thick, individually wrapped in plastic

notes.text: Weigh portions for even tartlets — scale is more reliable than eyeballing 12 pieces.
Freeze any discs you won't bake today — keeps up to 1 month. Thaw in refrigerator before rolling.
Leftover dough and scraps from rolling make simple cookies.

states.title: Chill Dough
states.direction: Chill wrapped discs in refrigerator for at least 2 hours or overnight.
states.exit_condition: Dough is firm and cold throughout — holds its shape when pressed

states.title: Roll Out Dough
states.direction: Place a chilled dough disc on a lightly floured surface. Roll to 3mm thick, rolling from center toward edge in all directions. Lift and rotate dough a quarter turn after every few strokes, dusting underneath as needed. Work quickly to keep dough cool. Cut circles sized for your tartlet pans.
states.exit_condition: Dough rolled to uniform 3mm thickness, circles cut for tartlet pans

notes.text: If dough becomes too soft to work with, return to refrigerator for a few minutes to firm up.
This dough may be rolled out multiple times without losing quality — a valuable property.

states.title: Line Tart Pan
states.direction: Line each tartlet pan: transfer dough circles, ease into bottom and sides, pressing gently into place. Do not stretch the dough. Patch any tears with extra dough, pressing firmly to adhere. Trim level with pan edges. Freeze remaining dough and scraps for future use.
states.exit_condition: All tartlet pans lined with dough, no gaps or tears, excess trimmed flush with rims

notes.text: Do not stretch the dough or the sides will shrink during baking.
For tartlets, you can press the dough disc directly into the pan with your fingers instead of rolling — push from center outward, working up the sides to an even thickness.

states.title: Chill Lined Shell
states.direction: Place pastry shell in refrigerator or freezer until firm, about 15 minutes.
states.exit_condition: Shell is firm to the touch — dough does not dent when lightly pressed

states.title: Preheat Oven
states.direction: Preheat oven to 325°F (160°C).
states.exit_condition: Oven at 325°F (160°C)

states.title: Dock & Partial Bake
states.direction: Dock the bottom of each chilled shell with fork tines or knife tip, making tiny holes about 5cm apart. Place in oven and bake 5 to 7 minutes for tartlets (7-10 min for a large shell).
states.exit_condition: Pastry is lightly colored, looks dry and opaque — not yet golden

notes.text: Check shell during baking and rotate pan if necessary for even color.

states.title: Egg Wash Shell
states.direction: Beat 1 egg with a pinch of salt in a small bowl. A minute or two before the desired partial-bake color is reached, remove shell from oven and lightly brush bottom and sides with egg wash. Return to oven and bake until coating is set.
states.exit_condition: Egg wash coating is set and sealed — surface looks glossy and firm

notes.text: The egg wash creates a moisture barrier that keeps the crust crisp longer under the wet filling.

states.title: Bake to Golden Brown
states.direction: Continue baking until shell is golden brown, about 5 minutes longer after egg wash.
states.exit_condition: Shell is uniformly golden brown — fully baked, not pale or raw-looking

states.title: Cool Shell Completely
states.direction: Remove from oven and let cool completely on a wire rack.
states.exit_condition: Shell is room temperature throughout — no warmth when touching the bottom

notes.text: Start making the lemon cream while the shell cools.

states.title: Strain Lemon Juice
states.direction: Strain 175g fresh lemon juice through a fine-mesh sieve to remove pulp and seeds.
states.exit_condition: Lemon juice strained, no pulp or seeds remain

states.title: Set Up Water Bath
states.direction: Pour water to a depth of about 5cm into the saucepan. Place over medium heat and bring to a simmer.
states.exit_condition: Water at a steady simmer in saucepan

notes.text: Never use unlined aluminum — acid reacts with metal and creates a metallic flavor.

states.title: Combine Curd Ingredients
states.direction: In the stainless-steel bowl: whisk 3 eggs and 1 egg yolk together first. Add 175g sugar and whisk immediately — do not let yolks and sugar sit. Add strained lemon juice and salt, whisk to combine.
states.exit_condition: All curd ingredients whisked together in steel bowl, homogeneous

notes.text: Never let egg yolks and sugar sit together without stirring — the sugar will 'cook' the yolks and turn them granular.

states.title: Cook Curd to 180°F (82°C)
states.direction: Place bowl over saucepan — it should rest on the rim, over but not touching the water. Whisk continuously until mixture becomes very thick and registers 180°F (82°C) on a thermometer. This will take 10 to 12 minutes.
states.exit_condition: Curd is very thick and thermometer reads 180°F (82°C)

states.title: Strain Curd
states.direction: Immediately strain the hot curd through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl to remove any chalazae or bits of cooked egg.
states.exit_condition: Curd is smooth and silky — no lumps, strands, or cooked egg bits remain

notes.text: Strain while hot — it flows through the sieve much more easily than when cooled.

states.title: Cool Curd to 140°F (60°C)
states.direction: Let strained curd cool to 140°F (60°C), stirring from time to time to release heat. Meanwhile, cut 225g butter into ~14g (1 Tbsp) pieces.
states.exit_condition: Curd temperature at 140°F (60°C), butter cut into 1 Tbsp pieces and ready

notes.text: Do not add butter while curd is too hot — the emulsion won't hold properly.

reminders.prompt: Record curd temperature before adding butter

states.title: Mount Butter into Cream
states.direction: Using immersion blender in the bowl, add 225g butter one tablespoon at a time, blending after each addition until incorporated before adding the next piece.
states.exit_condition: Cream is pale yellow, opaque, and quite thick — all butter incorporated and emulsified

notes.text: This 'mounting' technique (like a beurre blanc) keeps butter in emulsion, creating the softer, lighter texture that distinguishes this from standard lemon curd.
If the butter 'breaks' (comes out of emulsion), the cream won't be as light but will still taste delicious.

states.title: Fill Tart Shell
states.direction: Pour or spoon lemon cream into each cooled tartlet shell. Shake pans gently to smooth the surface.
states.exit_condition: All tartlet shells filled with lemon cream, surfaces smooth and level

notes.text: If using chilled lemon cream from storage, soften it first in a bowl over simmering water, stirring constantly to keep the emulsion.

states.title: Chill Until Set
states.direction: Chill the filled tart in the refrigerator until firm, about 2 hours.
states.exit_condition: Filling is firm — holds its shape when pan is tilted slightly. Keeps up to 3 days refrigerated.

states.title: Whip Cream
states.direction: Whip 240g very cold heavy cream until thickened. Add 8g sugar and whip until the cream holds soft peaks.
states.exit_condition: Cream holds soft peaks — billowy and just holding its shape, not stiff

states.title: Top & Serve
states.direction: Top the chilled tart with the whipped cream. Decorate with fresh flowers or candied fennel.
states.exit_condition: Tart topped with whipped cream and garnished. Ready to serve.

methods.detail: Refrigerate up to 3 days. Add whipped cream just before serving.
Well wrapped, refrigerator up to 1 week or freezer up to 2 weeks.
Sealed container, refrigerator up to 5 days. Re-soften over simmering water, whisking to maintain emulsion.
Wrapped in plastic, freezer up to 1 month. Thaw in refrigerator before rolling.
